overview: Restormel Castle is a striking ruin just outside Lostwithiel: a huge, almost perfectly round keep standing on a high mound with a deep ditch, looking down over the River Fowey. It dates from the later 13th century and was at its grandest under Edward the Black Prince, who stayed here twice.
It’s an easy, peaceful visit run by English Heritage: climb the steps to walk round the battlements, trace the outline of the great hall, then have a picnic on the grass with views over the valley.

expect.title: The round keep
expect.text: Walk the battlements of the circular keep for views over the countryside.

expect.title: Inside the walls
expect.text: Trace the great hall and other rooms the Black Prince used.

expect.title: For children
expect.text: A family trail to build your own forest.

goodToKnow.label: Parking
goodToKnow.text: Plenty of free parking about 70 metres from the entrance.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: About a mile and a half north of Lostwithiel, off the A390.

goodToKnow.label: Without a car
goodToKnow.text: The nearest bus stop is in Lostwithiel, then a walk of just over a mile along a minor road.

week.text: A short, scenic stop to combine with Lanhydrock or a wander round Lostwithiel’s antique shops. It also makes a good base for walks along the Fowey valley.

a small historic town on the Fowey
forest trails a short drive away

tips: Bring a picnic: the castle lawns have lovely views.
